drhp.business: The Company operates in the Jute Industry, manufacturing jute goods including B twill sacking bags, jute shopping bags and yarn at its mills in eastern India. Demand is anchored by the Government of India's Jute Packing Order, under which food grains have to be packed 100% in jute bags and sugar 20% in jute bags, alongside increasing world-wide awareness of environment-friendly natural products which has lifted demand for jute shopping bags. The Company also pursues value-added and diversified products for export markets.

risks.note: Raw jute prices rose to the highest level ever in the history of the jute industry in FY2025-26 on lower crop output, and the non-availability and/or irregular supply of raw jute adversely affected the running of the mills. Raw fibre is the dominant input, so crop-driven price and supply swings pass straight into cost of manufacture and mill running.

The Jute Packing Order (100% jute packing for food grains, 20% for sugar) is the demand anchor and management lists 'Buying of Jute Bags by Government of India' as its first opportunity, while flagging as a threat 'Lower demand of jute bags by Government of India if monsoon is deficit' -- a single administrative buyer whose offtake is tied to the crop.
risks.risk: Dependence on Government of India demand for jute bags

risks.note: Both sides of the business turn on the crop cycle: a deficit monsoon cuts Government demand for bags, while crop output drives raw jute prices. The outlook itself is conditioned on 'the weather also being favorable' for the ensuing season.

Management lists 'Shortage of workers increasing' as its first threat. Jute manufacturing is labour-intensive and mills in the eastern region depend on workmen availability, so a tightening labour pool constrains production and utilisation.

'Strong competition from Bangladesh whose labour and fiber are cheaper than India' -- Bangladesh is the world's second-largest jute producer after India and its structurally lower input and labour costs cap realisations, particularly in non-mandated and export segments.

The Company operates solely in the jute industry with no change in the nature of business during the year, and the industry is concentrated in the eastern region of India. There is no disclosed diversification outside jute goods, so every risk above hits the whole business at once.

Management itself frames 'Substantial decrease in prices of Raw Jute leading to reduction in prices of finished goods' as an opportunity, but the same mechanism deflates realisations and can devalue inventory carried at higher raw jute cost -- relevant given the Company spent the year reducing old stock.
risks.risk: Finished-goods price deflation from falling raw material prices

risks.note: Implementation and administration of the Board-approved Risk Management Framework are entrusted to the Executive Director cum CFO, with periodic review by the Audit Committee and the Board, and internal audit is outsourced to M/s. Vimal & Seksaria, Chartered Accountants. The Board states that, based on the assessment of risks in the financial statements and MD&A, none of the risks currently identified appears to pose any significant existential threat to the Company.
risks.risk: Concentration of the risk-management function and reliance on internal audit
